issues.description: The problem statement (UML and method list) specifies orderMeal(Meal): void (no return value), but the reference solution implements orderMeal(Meal) as returning boolean. This mismatch in the method return type can confuse students about the expected signature and whether they should return a value or not.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to allow a boolean return and describe its meaning (e.g., success/failure), or change the reference implementation to a void return type (and adjust its return usage). Also ensure the template usage and examples match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but it also requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is contradictory and may confuse students about where to initialize the static final stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the initialization instructions: either state that only instance attributes (like orders) must be initialized in the constructor and that static/shared attributes (like stock) should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, or change the requirement so that stock is not static if it must be initialized in the instance constructor. Update the problem statement accordingly so students are not led to attempt assigning a static final field in an instance constructor.
